title: ElasticZRAM: Revisiting ZRAM for Swapping on Mobile Devices
problem: Mobile devices use two-level memory swapping with ZRAM and storage, but ZRAM trades off memory consumption and CPU cycles against reducing storage writes. Traditional fixed ZRAM policies don't adapt to application behavior and device characteristics.
motivation: Optimizing ZRAM allocation improves application responsiveness and reduces resource consumption on memory-constrained mobile devices.
method: ElasticZRAM dynamically adjusts ZRAM allocation and compression policies based on application characteristics and NAND flash storage properties. The system adapts memory tier management to optimize the tradeoff between CPU overhead, memory usage, and storage I/O traffic.
key_novelty: Elastic, application-aware ZRAM management that adapts compression and allocation policies based on workload behavior and storage device characteristics.
contributions: Proposes ElasticZRAM architecture with dynamic, adaptive ZRAM management
Incorporates awareness of application characteristics and NAND flash device properties
Demonstrates up to 24.8% improvement in application response time with negligible overhead on Google Pixel 6
primary_theme: elastic memory swapping for mobile devices
